RFP No. 2027-014  –  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park Building CustodialIssued October 5, 2026
City of Ashby Creek, Missouri  |  RFP No. 2027-014  |  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park CustodialSection 1 – General Information

Section 1 – General Information

1.1 Purpose. The City of Ashby Creek, Missouri (the “City”), through its Department of Parks, Recreation and Forestry (the “Department”), is soliciting proposals from qualified firms to furnish all labor, supervision, equipment, fuel, materials and transportation necessary to perform turf mowing, trimming, edging, litter removal, athletic field mowing, planting bed and tree maintenance at the City parks and municipal sites listed in Attachment A, Table A-1; turf mowing and litter removal on the medians and rights-of-way listed in Attachment A, Table A-2; and custodial services for the park buildings listed in Attachment C, Table C-1. One (1) contract will be awarded for all services.

1.2 Term of Contract. The initial term of the Contract shall be two (2) years, commencing March 1, 2027 and ending February 28, 2029. Upon mutual written agreement and subject to annual appropriation, the Contract may be renewed for up to three (3) additional one (1) year terms, for a maximum total term of five (5) years. Pricing shall remain firm for the initial term. Any request for a price adjustment at renewal shall be submitted in writing not less than ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term and shall not exceed the change in the CPI-U (Midwest Region) for the preceding twelve (12) months.

1.3 Current Services. Park and right-of-way mowing is presently performed under Contract No. PR-2022-031, awarded in February 2022 to Halvorsen Turf Management, LLC, which expires February 28, 2027 at the end of its final renewal term. The City’s annual cost under that contract for calendar year 2025 was $612,480. Custodial service for the park buildings in Attachment C is currently performed by City staff and is not part of Contract No. PR-2022-031. This information is provided for reference only and does not represent a guaranteed level of compensation under the new Contract.

1.4 Pre-Proposal Meeting and Site Tour. A non-mandatory pre-proposal meeting will be held on the date shown on the cover page. Proposers are strongly encouraged to visit every site; site conditions, slopes, obstacles and access restrictions are the Proposer’s responsibility. Failure to inspect a site will not relieve the Contractor of the obligation to perform the work.

1.5 Questions and Addenda. All questions shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to the Purchasing Agent by the deadline on the cover page. Answers and any changes to this RFP will be issued only by written addendum. Proposers shall acknowledge each addendum on Form 2 and in the transmittal letter (Section 4.2, Tab 1). Where an addendum changes a quantity in Attachment A or Attachment C, the addendum governs.

1.6 Basis of Payment. Mowing shall be paid per completed cycle per site at the unit prices on Attachment B, based on the Mowable Turf Acres stated in Table A-1 and the median and right-of-way dimensions stated in Table A-2. Custodial services shall be paid as a fixed monthly price per building. Quantities are the City’s best estimate; the City does not guarantee any minimum number of cycles. Sites may be added or deleted during the term by written change order at the unit prices.

1.7 Evaluation. Proposals will be evaluated on (a) price, 40 points; (b) experience with municipal park and right-of-way maintenance of comparable scope, 25 points; (c) staffing, equipment and work plan, 25 points; and (d) references, 10 points. The City reserves the right to reject any or all proposals and to waive informalities.

1.8 Insurance and Prevailing Wage. The Contractor shall maintain the insurance coverages stated in Section 5.1. Work under this Contract is not subject to the Missouri prevailing wage law (Sections 290.210 – 290.340, RSMo) except as may apply to any construction-type additional work ordered by change order.

RFP No. 2027-014  –  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park Building CustodialIssued October 5, 2026
City of Ashby Creek, Missouri  |  RFP No. 2027-014  |  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park CustodialSection 2 – Scope of Services

Section 2 – Scope of Services: Grounds

2.1 Definitions.

  1. Mowing Cycle – one complete mowing of every turf area at a site, including trimming around all obstacles, edging of hard surfaces, removal of litter before mowing, and blowing of clippings off walks, drives, parking lots and courts. A cycle is complete only when every task is done at the entire site.
  2. Total Site Acres – the approximate gross area of the site from the City GIS parcel layer. It includes building footprints, paved areas, water bodies, wooded areas, natural areas and ballfields, and is provided for information only.
  3. Mowable Turf Acres – the turf area mowed each cycle at the Service Level shown. It excludes ballfield acres, rough-mow acres, planting beds, paving, water and woods. Mowable Turf Acres are the basis of payment.
  4. Rough Mow Acres – natural areas, meadow edges, drainage swales and firebreaks maintained at Service Level 3.
  5. Ballfield Acres – the turf infield and outfield of the listed baseball, softball, soccer and multipurpose fields, maintained under Section 2.5 and not included in Mowable Turf Acres.

2.2 Service Levels. Each site and area is assigned one of the following Service Levels:

Service LevelDescription and standardMowing heightCycle / estimated cycles per season
1 – Improved TurfHigh-visibility parks, plazas, municipal building grounds, medians and rights-of-way. Finish-mowed with rotary or reel mowers; trimmed and edged every cycle; no scalping, rutting or windrows.2½ – 3½ in.7-day cycle; estimated 30 cycles (March 15 – November 15)
2 – Semi-Improved TurfNeighborhood and pocket parks, greenway lawns, cemetery and lower-visibility municipal lots. Rotary-mowed; trimmed every cycle and edged every other cycle.3 – 4 in.14-day cycle; estimated 17 cycles
3 – Rough Mow (Unimproved)Natural areas, meadow paths, swales and firebreaks. Tractor-mounted rotary or flail mower; no trimming except around signs and benches.6 – 8 in.6 cycles per season (May – October)

2.3 Mowing Season and Scheduling. The mowing season is March 15 through November 15. The Department may suspend or add cycles for drought, saturated soils or rapid growth; any cycle not performed will not be paid. The Contractor shall submit a weekly route schedule by Thursday for the following week. Sites with scheduled events (Table A-1, Sites 1, 2, 3 and 10) shall be mowed no later than 24 hours before the event.

2.4 Litter Removal. Litter, debris, limbs under 4 in. diameter and pet waste shall be removed from all turf, beds, parking lots and walks at the frequency shown in the “Litter Pickup Frequency” column of Table A-1 and the “Litter Pickup” column of Table A-2, and in every case before mowing. “Each cycle” means once per mowing cycle. Park trash receptacles are emptied by City staff except at Sites 3 and 10, where the Contractor shall empty receptacles at each litter visit.

2.5 Athletic Fields. Ballfield turf (Table A-1, “Ballfields” columns) shall be mowed twice weekly from April 1 through October 31 at 2 – 2½ in. and once every 14 days at other times during the season. Infield skin grooming, lining and base installation are performed by Department staff and are not part of this Contract.

RFP No. 2027-014  –  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park Building CustodialIssued October 5, 2026
City of Ashby Creek, Missouri  |  RFP No. 2027-014  |  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park CustodialSection 2 – Scope of Services

2.6 Planting Beds. Planting beds (square feet as stated in Table A-1) shall be kept free of weeds and litter at each visit, re-edged in April and September, and top-dressed once per year with 2 in. of shredded hardwood mulch furnished and installed by the Contractor. Seasonal color at Sites 10 and 17 is planted by the Department; the Contractor maintains it.

2.7 Trees. Tree counts in Table A-1 are trees within or adjoining mowed turf. The Contractor shall maintain 3-ft mulch rings, remove root suckers and water sprouts to 8 ft, and remove fallen limbs. Pruning above 12 ft and removals are excluded and will be performed by the City Forester. Median street trees noted in Table A-2 receive the same care.

2.8 Medians and Rights-of-Way. Turf medians and roadside rights-of-way listed in Table A-2 are maintained to Service Level 1 on a 7-day cycle; Segment M-5 is paved and is not mowed (Table A-2, note 3/). Areas are stated as a length in linear feet (LF) and an average width in feet; “Sides” = 2 means both sides of the roadway are maintained to the stated width. Widths are measured back-of-curb to back-of-curb for raised medians and back-of-curb (or edge of pavement) to the right-of-way line for roadside segments. The Contractor shall furnish traffic control in accordance with the MUTCD, Part 6, for all median work.

2.9 Chemical Application. Selective post-emergent herbicide for broadleaf weeds may be applied twice per season to Service Level 1 turf by a Missouri-certified commercial applicator. No herbicide, pesticide or fertilizer shall be applied at Site 15 (Cedar Hollow Nature Preserve) or within 25 ft of any lake or stream. Joint weed control on paved areas shall be by hand pulling, string trimmer or a non-selective herbicide labeled for hardscape.

2.10 Damage. The Contractor shall repair, at its own cost, any damage to irrigation heads, signs, monuments, trees, benches, play equipment or turf caused by its operations within 72 hours of notice.

2.11 Quality Control and Inspection. The Department will inspect each site within 48 hours after a cycle is reported complete. Deficiencies shall be corrected within 24 hours at no cost. Two uncorrected deficiencies at the same site in one month will result in non-payment of that cycle.

2.12 Paved Areas. Paved areas are maintained under this Section as follows: (a) walks, drives, parking lots and courts at the sites in Table A-1 are blown clear at each mowing cycle and policed at each litter visit; they are not separately measured or priced; (b) the stamped concrete and paver median on Segment M-5 (Table A-2) receives weekly litter removal and joint weed control and is priced per visit on Attachment B; and (c) the picnic shelter and gazebo slabs listed in Table C-2 are blown off, and tables wiped, at each litter visit at the host site (Section 3.3). Snow and ice removal is not part of this Contract.

Section 3 – Scope of Services: Park Building Custodial

3.1 General. The Contractor shall clean, disinfect and restock the park buildings in Attachment C, Table C-1, on the days stated. All restroom facilities shall be cleaned and in operation no later than the time stated in the Service Window column, including holidays where stated. Paper products, hand soap and trash liners are furnished by the Contractor.

3.2 Tasks. Each service shall include: cleaning and disinfecting toilets, urinals, lavatories, showers, partitions and drinking fountains; sanitizing door handles, push plates and light switches; spot-cleaning walls; sweeping and wet-mopping all floors with a neutral disinfectant; emptying trash; restocking; and reporting vandalism or plumbing failures to the Department by 10:00 a.m. Community Center (PB-1) service additionally includes vacuuming carpet, dust-mopping the gymnasium floor and cleaning the catering kitchen counters (not appliances). Gymnasium floor refinishing is excluded.

3.3 Picnic Shelters. Open-air picnic shelters (Table C-2) are not buildings for custodial purposes. Shelter slabs shall be blown off and tables wiped as part of the litter visit at the host site (Section 2.12(c)).

3.4 Supplies and Keys. The Department will issue keys for PB-1 through PB-4 at the start of the Contract. The Contractor shall lock PB-2 and PB-4 at dusk (no later than 9:00 p.m.) and unlock them before the service window. Lost keys will be re-cored at the Contractor’s expense.

City of Ashby Creek, Missouri  |  RFP No. 2027-014  |  Park, Median & ROW Mowing and Park CustodialSections 4 – 5

Section 4 – Proposal Submission Requirements

4.1 Delivery. Submit one (1) signed original, three (3) copies and one (1) electronic copy (searchable PDF on a USB flash drive) in a sealed envelope or box, labeled as shown on the cover page, by the due date and time. Proposals received after that time will not be opened. Proposals submitted by fax or e-mail will not be accepted.

4.2 Format. Proposals shall be organized behind numbered tabs as follows:

  • Tab 1 – Transmittal letter signed by an officer authorized to bind the firm, acknowledging each addendum by number and date.
  • Tab 2 – Firm profile: years in business, office location, and not less than three (3) years of municipal park or right-of-way maintenance experience.
  • Tab 3 – Staffing plan: on-site supervisor, crew assignments, organization chart and resumes of key personnel.
  • Tab 4 – Equipment list (owned or leased, with model year) dedicated to this Contract.
  • Tab 5 – Work plan: route plan by cycle, quality control procedures and response to Department work orders.
  • Tab 6 – Three (3) references for comparable work performed within the past five (5) years (Form 3).
  • Tab 7 – Attachment B, Price Proposal Form (all lines completed).
  • Tab 8 – Form 1, Form 2, IRS Form W-9, and a sample certificate of insurance showing the coverages in Section 5.1.

4.3 Proposal Validity. Proposals shall remain firm for ninety (90) days after the opening date.

4.4 Licenses. Before execution the successful Proposer shall hold a City business license, and each herbicide applicator a Missouri commercial applicator certification (ornamental and turf).

4.5 Communication. From the date of issue until award, Proposers shall communicate about this RFP only with the Purchasing Agent, in writing.

4.6 Public Records. Proposals become public records under the Missouri Sunshine Law (Chapter 610, RSMo) after a contract is executed or all proposals are rejected. Mark any page the Proposer considers proprietary.

Section 5 – General Contract Terms

5.1 Insurance. Before starting work, and for the full term, the Contractor shall maintain and furnish certificates for the following, naming the City, its officials and employees as additional insureds on the liability policies: Commercial General Liability, $1,000,000 each occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate; Business Automobile Liability, $1,000,000 combined single limit; Workers’ Compensation at statutory limits (Chapter 287, RSMo) with Employer’s Liability of $500,000 each accident; and Umbrella or Excess Liability, $2,000,000.

5.2 Invoicing and Payment. Invoice monthly, by the tenth (10th) day of the following month, by site, segment and building. The City pays approved invoices within thirty (30) days.

5.3 Work Authorization. As required by Section 285.530, RSMo, as a condition of the award of any contract in excess of five thousand dollars, the Contractor shall affirm by sworn affidavit (Form 1) and documentation its enrollment and participation in a federal work authorization program with respect to the employees working in connection with the contracted services, and that it does not knowingly employ any person who is an unauthorized alien in connection with those services.

5.4 Anti-Discrimination Against Israel Act. If the Contractor has ten (10) or more employees and the Contract is valued at $100,000 or more, the Contractor certifies under Section 34.600, RSMo, that it is not currently engaged in, and shall not for the duration of the Contract engage in, a boycott of goods or services from the State of Israel (Form 2).

5.5 Termination. The City may terminate the Contract for convenience on thirty (30) days’ written notice, or for cause if a default is not cured within ten (10) days after written notice.

CITY OF ASHBY CREEK, MISSOURI – PURCHASING DIVISION
ADDENDUM NO. 1
RFP No. 2027-014 – Park, Median and Right-of-Way Mowing, Grounds Maintenance and Park Building Custodial Services
Date of Addendum: October 19, 2026  •  Proposal due date is UNCHANGED: November 6, 2026, 2:00 p.m. CT

This Addendum forms a part of the Contract Documents and modifies the original RFP as noted below. Proposers shall acknowledge receipt of this Addendum on Form 2. Failure to acknowledge may result in disqualification. Where this Addendum conflicts with the RFP, this Addendum governs.

A. Changes to Attachment A, Table A-1 (Park and Municipal Site Schedule)

  1. Site 14, Wexford Commons Pocket Park, is DELETED in its entirety. Ownership transfers to the Wexford Commons Homeowners Association effective January 1, 2027. Delete all quantities for Site 14 (0.48 mowable turf acres, 320 SF planting beds, 9 trees). Do not price Site 14 on Attachment B.
  2. Site 9, Creekside Greenway: Mowable Turf Acres are REVISED from 6.40 to 7.15 acres (trailhead lawn expansion completed August 2026). Rough Mow Acres (18.60) are unchanged.

B. Changes to Attachment A, Table A-2 (Median and Right-of-Way Mowing Schedule)

  1. Segment M-6, Kingsridge Road: Limits are REVISED to read “Pioneer Drive to Westfield Boulevard.” Length is REVISED from 2,640 LF to 3,180 LF. Average width (14 FT) and Sides (1) are unchanged.

C. Changes to Attachment C, Table C-1 (Park Building Custodial Schedule)

  1. PB-3, Sports Complex Restroom and Concession Building: a family restroom addition (180 gross SF) at the east end of the building was completed in September 2026. Gross SF is REVISED from 2,240 to 2,420; Cleanable SF is REVISED from 1,960 to 2,130; Restroom Fixtures are REVISED from 8 / 3 / 6 / 0 to 9 / 3 / 7 / 0. Cleaning days are unchanged.

D. Questions Received and Answers

Q1. Will the City accept proposals by e-mail?
A1. No. See Section 4.1.

Q2. Are the Ballfield Acres in Table A-1 included in the Mowable Turf Acres?
A2. No. See Section 2.1(c) and (e).

Q3. Will the City provide acreage for the medians in Table A-2?
A3. No. See Table A-2, note 1/.

Q4. Are any of the medians irrigated?
A4. Yes, M-1 and M-2. The City maintains the systems. The Contractor shall flag heads before the first cycle and is responsible for damage under Section 2.10.

Addendum No. 1, Part D (continued)

Q5. Who is the current contractor and what does the City spend per year?
A5. Halvorsen Turf Management, LLC, under Contract No. PR-2022-031 (Section 1.3). The $612,480 annual cost for 2025 is for mowing only. Segments R-3 and R-4 are new with this RFP, and the park buildings are cleaned by City staff today.

Q6. Can the City provide the bid tabulation from the 2022 solicitation?
A6. Bid tabulations are public records and may be requested from the City Clerk under Chapter 610, RSMo.

Q7. Is the Contractor responsible for cleaning the Old Mill Park restroom (PB-5)?
A7. No. See Table C-1, note 2/.

Q8. Is a bid bond or performance bond required?
A8. No.

Q9. What is the total possible length of the Contract?
A9. Five (5) years, if all renewals are exercised (Section 1.2).

All other terms and conditions of RFP No. 2027-014 remain unchanged.
